speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
text: asked the Minister for Manpower regarding migrant workers living in dormitories (a) from January to October 2021, how many (i) sought mental health care and (ii) had to stop work temporarily due to severe mental health concerns; (b) how does the data compare to that of 2020 and 2019; (c) whether the Ministry has conducted any research or survey to ascertain the mental well-being of these workers; and (d) what are the efforts to further manage their mental health as many of these workers are still unable to leave the dormitories.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We are sparing no efforts to strengthen the mental health support ecosystem for them.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Since last November, when we initiated the Project DAWN task force, DAWN has worked with our non-government organisation (NGO) partners, healthcare partners, employers and dormitory operators to develop such an ecosystem to look out for migrant workers, to listen to their concerns, to identify those who need more support, as well as link them with the appropriate care channels.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: First, we are raising the awareness of mental health issues and we are broadening the outreach of training in basic mental health and psychological first aid, or PFA.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Second, we are working with our NGO partners to make counselling and para-counselling more accessible.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Third, mental healthcare has been made even more accessible.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Any migrant worker identified to have need for or to benefit from mental healthcare will be linked up with the appropriate services, including the counselling hotlines.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In particular, an escalation pathway with the Institute of Mental Health (IMH) has been developed to ensure timely care for more severe cases when necessary.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Nonetheless, any easing of movement restrictions will need to be done in a careful and calibrated manner, so as not to trade one stress for another.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In particular, as you have heard in Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary's Ministerial Statement yesterday about our healthcare system, we have to be mindful that we do not treat the stress of one where there is some restriction of movement for our migrant workers, to overwhelming that of our healthcare system.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have also removed pre-visit testing requirements for vaccinated migrant workers, which benefits more than 98% of the dormitory population.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Concurrently, we are working with RC operators and community partners to introduce programmes and new offerings to make the RC visits more engaging.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have also recently expanded community visits from 500 to 3,000 vaccinated migrant workers per week.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have expanded to include Geylang Serai or Joo Chiat, in addition to Little India.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have also extended the visit duration to eight hours at each time.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Members of the House, we remain committed towards caring for our migrant workers' mental well-being through a good support system, as well as to continue to ease measures safely.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: MOM will continue to monitor the mental health of migrant workers by working closely with our partners.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Minister mentioned that we are ramping up psychological first aid training.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Specifically, is this peer support training for migrant workers to provide support for each other, or is this support for employers to provide a more supportive workplace environment, in terms of mental wellness, or is it both?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Indeed, we approach this training on a very holistic manner because mental health awareness, the ability to be able to identify and escalate very quickly and to do constant surveillance and constant monitoring and engagement is a multi-disciplinary, multi-pronged approach that is needed through the support of dorm operators, by our FAST ambassadors on the ground, by the employers, by the NGOs, the partners and, of course, ultimately, the tertiary healthcare providers, including IMH.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We have a multi-pronged approach when we started Project DAWN last year.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: DAWN is an acronym. "D" stands for depression, "A" stands for awareness, "W" is wellness and the "N" stands for normalisation, how do we help the migrant workers normalise back.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The DAWN task force started with seven core initiatives.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: They are grouped according to primary prevention, secondary intervention and the third part, not really tertiary, but where we help them to rehabilitate back into society.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As a result of that, we have got buddies, we have also worked with volunteers.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, it is a multi-pronged approach to reach out to all of our migrant workers who need help.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: But I think, given the amount of Parliamentary Questions (PQs) that we have to cover today, I will leave it at that.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I have one supplementary question for the Minister.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Minister spoke about the pilot, which saw an increase in numbers from 500 to 3,000.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Can the Minister share with the House what were the considerations that determined that number 3,000?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Why not 2,000 or 4,000, because that will give the public and those who are looking at this issue more closely some ideas as to when further opening can potentially take place or, at the very least, when certain foreign workers who may need a little bit more assistance can be attended to by the relevant agencies and individuals?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The question of easing the restrictions for our migrant workers to go out into the community is constantly on our minds, not just all of us in MOM, particularly the ACE Group.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: At different times when we planned, with the drawer plans that we have in place, each time, we were hit by different curve balls.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: You would have read about the Delta variant.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: At any particular point in time where we try to ramp up, easing the restrictions, there were new and significant turns of events that did not allow us to do so.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We then focused on the singular approach of ensuring that all of our migrant workers are protected through vaccination.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The vaccination centres were set up and our focus was really making sure that we protect them.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: When we were able to bring them up to a high level of vaccination within the dorms, again, we tried to work on a mechanism for easing.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In my earlier interview with The Straits Times and with the media, I said, "The key thing was finding a safe and a very calibrated manner".

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And I think that there were obviously subsequent events that have overtaken us.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In spite of that, once we have achieved that high level of vaccination, and we also had enough evidence to show that those of us who have received and completed the two doses of the vaccination, the incidence of complications was significantly less than for those who are unvaccinated.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We also sought feedback through our survey with the migrant workers to ask them what would be important for them when they go out to visit these community areas.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Many of them wanted to go to a religious place of worship.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, our ACE Group then engaged the Hindu temples, the mosques, as well as churches to see how we could accommodate them to let them fulfil their religious needs.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We also worked with the shopkeepers and so on.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We identified shopkeepers, the retail shops to make sure that social distancing was adequately maintained.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We reached out to the churches, the temples, the mosques to get them to support us and we started that pilot visit.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We also had to ensure, as we move towards endemicity, at some point, we were concerned about, given the space that they are living in, to ensure that the infection, if it comes into the dorm, it does not spread.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, we took all the necessary precautions in terms of pre-event testing before they left.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And after coming back, we also tested them.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: At each step of the way, there were quite a fair bit of logistical arrangements that we had to make, including arranging for the buses to bring them there; also making sure that the itinerary, the programmes planned for them were adequate.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In the beginning, we even had to nudge employers, because even though we opened up 500 a week, we found that, for a while, we were only getting about 50% to 60% of them coming on board.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: There were also migrant workers who signed up, only to cancel at the last minute.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, these are all the logistical issues and so on that we had to plan through.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Once we were able to smoothen out all of these different gaps and so on, we then moved on to increasing the number to 3,000.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: At this particular point in time, because we had just started the 3,000 last weekend, just about three days ago, we will maintain and watch it for a while.
